subsystems.name: Radioisotope power source
subsystems.role: supplies electricity for decades in darkness, far beyond solar panel range.

subsystems.name: Propulsion and trajectory hardware
subsystems.role: gets the craft onto a fast escape path rather than a slow coast.
parts: solid kick motor (for a close solar pass)

subsystems.name: Thermal protection
subsystems.role: survives a planned pass close to the Sun if a solar gravity assist is used.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: returns a usable signal from hundreds of astronomical units away.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: samples the interstellar medium directly instead of inferring it.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus and autonomy
subsystems.role: keeps a crewless craft working without intervention for 50 years.

buildSteps.title: Fix the science case and trajectory
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose between a Jupiter gravity assist and a far faster solar Oberth manoeuvre, which decides how much mass the spacecraft can carry.

buildSteps.title: Make the power source
buildSteps.detail: Plutonium-238 oxide is pressed into ceramic pellets, encapsulated, and assembled into a generator with thermocouples that convert its heat to electricity; units are tested to destruction before flight.

buildSteps.title: Build the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Each sensor is designed for the particles, fields and dust it will meet outside the heliosphere, then vacuum-tested and calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Structure, propulsion, communications dish and instruments are integrated onto a mass-constrained bus.

buildSteps.title: Environmental test
buildSteps.detail: The whole craft is shaken on a vibration table and cycled through vacuum and temperature extremes to prove it can survive launch and cruise.

buildSteps.title: Load the power source and launch
buildSteps.detail: The generator is attached at the launch site, the craft is encapsulated, and a heavy-lift rocket sends it onto an escape trajectory.

buildSteps.title: Gravity assists
buildSteps.detail: A planetary flyby — and optionally a close solar pass behind a heat shield — bends the path and adds the speed needed to outrun the Sun's influence.

buildSteps.title: Cruise and cross the boundary
buildSteps.detail: After roughly 15 years the probe passes the heliopause, then keeps transmitting for decades while power output slowly falls.

prerequisites.why: spacecraft like the Voyagers and New Horizons prove the principle, but output halves roughly every 87 years, so the mission must fit its power budget.
large dishes and sensitive receivers are the only way to hear a weakening signal across hundreds of astronomical units.
solar observatory missions have flown through the Sun's corona behind carbon-composite shields, but never as part of an interstellar trajectory burn.

prerequisites.tech: High-energy upper stages and solid kick motors
prerequisites.why: the speed needed at launch is set by available rocket energy, not by the spacecraft.
light travel time means the craft must diagnose and recover from faults on its own for years.

pathway.milestone: concept studies and a designed architecture, with the Voyagers as the only craft to have crossed the heliopause
pathway.unlocks: a concrete mission baseline, mass and power budget, and instrument list.

pathway.milestone: technology maturation of the power source, thermal shield and payload
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the hardware will still work in the 2060s and beyond.

pathway.milestone: selection and launch, with a Jupiter or solar assist to reach escape velocity
pathway.unlocks: the fastest practical route out of the Sun's bubble.

pathway.milestone: heliopause crossing and a multi-decade cruise to several hundred astronomical units
pathway.unlocks: the first in-situ map of the interstellar medium and a true precursor to any future interstellar flight.
